ontology.note: Existing ontology alignment, plus the inclusion rule and outer margin now recorded as typed provenance so receipts produced under different rules cannot be mistaken for each other. fw:rasterMaskConvention is constrained by SHACL to a known identifier.

changes.description: Align the all-touched inclusion rule with GDAL ALL_TOUCHED, measured cell by cell against rasterio 1.5.2 and GDAL 3.12.2 in the Validation Lab: differences over a deliberately pixel-aligned cutline fall from 35 cells to 2, and the cropped window now agrees. The residual 2 cells come from GDAL burning cells along a cutline vertex lying exactly on a cell border, which is an artifact of its line rasterizer rather than a stateable rule. Records the convention and the outer margin in N3 evidence. See docs/experiments/29-raster-edge-inclusion.md.

Migration, no adapter required: All touched now includes a cell only when the cutline covers part of its area or crosses its interior. A cutline edge lying exactly on the border between two cells no longer pulls in the cell outside it, and the cropped window is no longer padded. Re-running a saved all-touched clip can therefore retain fewer boundary cells, and any total derived from one can change. Cell center inside is unaffected. Receipts from earlier runs carry no fw:rasterMaskConvention and were produced by the more inclusive rule.

evidence.note: Independently compared against rasterio 1.5.2 with GDAL 3.12.2 over a synthetic CRS84 grid and a concave, pixel-aligned cutline: cell centre inside agrees exactly; all touched differs by 2 of 146 cells, both GDAL-only and attributable to its line rasterizer. A unit test pins the convention at an exactly aligned border. The margin has no GDAL equivalent and is compared only against a dilation model, so it remains unvalidated. No claim is made about cartographic or scientific suitability.
